claims.statement: The webview's refine action refuses to run without a completed transcription or import result, mints a fresh job id with crypto.randomUUID(), and invokes refine_transcript(jobId, result.jobId, attendees.selectedIds()); selectedIds() returns only ids still present in the roster, in roster order.

Refinement runs under two job ids with different roles: the refinement's own id claims the single job slot, while the produced minutes are registered under the target transcription's id via register_minutes(target, ...), which is why open-minutes and reveal-output keep working from the original result.

refine_transcript performs everything that can fail cheaply before occupying the single job slot: target artifact lookup (ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND), trimmed settings load, attendee filtering, and the API key gate; only then does claim_with_id take the slot, refusing a concurrent job with BUSY and a reused id with JOB_ID_CONFLICT.

Only the selected attendees travel to refinement, filtered from the saved roster in roster order rather than selection order; the glossary is not selectable — every saved term is sent on every refinement as global correction context.

The assistant API key is deliberately excluded from ordinary settings reads (load_assistant returns api_key: None with only a boolean api_key_stored) and is read through load_assistant_api_key at the one moment refinement needs it; nothing stored fails with ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING before any process is spawned.

The minutes output path is a pure domain derivation: minutes_path strips a `_화자별` suffix from the transcript's stem and appends `_회의록.md`, making the minutes a sibling file of the transcript; the caller cannot choose a different location.

Minutes become addressable as an artifact only after register_minutes appends the path to the target's Artifacts entry: Artifacts::path_for(Minutes) returns None beforehand, so open_artifact(minutes) fails with ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND until registration succeeds.

Background text, the selected participant roster JSON, and glossary JSON are handed to the worker through 0600 temporary files (galpi-{kind}-{job_id} in the system temp dir) created with .mode(0o600) and .create_new(true) in one call — set at creation rather than chmod'ed afterwards so the roster is never briefly world-readable — and they are removed after the run regardless of outcome.

The assistant API key reaches the worker only through the GALPI_ASSISTANT_API_KEY environment variable — never the argument vector or a file — alongside optional GALPI_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL and GALPI_ASSISTANT_REASONING_EFFORT overrides; the worker reads the variable at refine start and refuses with InvalidInput when it is absent.

When the meeting has source audio, the host passes --meeting-date derived from the audio file's local mtime, because a recording is written once when the meeting ends so its timestamp is the meeting day, while the transcript's timestamp is whenever transcription ran; without the flag the worker falls back to the transcript file's own mtime.

The host spawns `<venv python> -m galpi_worker refine --transcript … --output …` (plus optional --background/--participants/--glossary/--model/--meeting-date) with worker_protocol parsing of every stdout JSONL line, and the run only counts as successful if exactly one Refined event arrived — a missing or duplicate completion event fails with WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR.

The worker-returned minutes path is contain-checked: both the transcript's meeting directory and the minutes path are canonicalized, and a minutes path outside the directory fails with WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR, so a compromised worker cannot point the host at an arbitrary file.

Cancelling a refinement escalates SIGTERM → SIGKILL after 3 seconds on the worker's process group and returns CANCELLED; the temporary context files are still removed because removal runs on every exit path of the adapter.

The worker runs refine under redirect_stdout(sys.stderr) so library prints cannot corrupt the protocol stream, and maps every failure to one error event plus an exit code: InvalidInput becomes error code INVALID_INPUT with exit 2, and any other exception becomes ENGINE_ERROR with exit 1.

Worker-side context parsing converts the host's participant and glossary JSON into typed records with required name/term fields (mirroring the host's trimming rules), and missing or blank context renders as explicit placeholder blocks (NO_BACKGROUND / NO_PARTICIPANTS / NO_GLOSSARY) that tell the model to rely on transcript evidence only, never a blank prompt section.

Refinement strategy is a pure function of transcript length: at most 48,000 characters go through one streaming request; longer transcripts are split only at whole speaker-turn line boundaries into chunks of at most 16,000 characters (an oversized turn stays whole), and every chunk after the first carries the previous chunk's last 400 characters as an `<이전구간끝>` preamble explicitly marked context-only.

The map pass extracts facts from chunks with three concurrent ThreadPoolExecutor workers, each streaming into a quiet EventWriter while the caller reports progress per completed chunk across the 35–68% band — a per-character count would jump backwards as concurrent streams overtook each other — and notes are reassembled in transcript order by chunk number; a single-chunk map pass streams within the whole band instead.

The reduce pass composes the final minutes in exactly one request using the normative system prompt over the ordered partial notes, instructed to merge duplicates, resolve decisions superseded by later chunks, and invent nothing absent from the notes, with streaming progress in the 70–88% band.

The finished minutes are published atomically — written to a `.tmp` sibling then replaced onto the output path, so no partial document is ever observable — and the `refined` protocol event names the output path, which is what the host uses as the result.

The assistant transport is stdlib-urllib OpenAI-compatible SSE: POST {base_url}/chat/completions with Accept: text/event-stream, stream: true, temperature 0.2, a 600-second timeout, default base URL https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4, default model glm-5.3-flash, max_tokens 131072 for GLM models on the default endpoint versus 32768 elsewhere, and reasoning_effort included only when set to low|medium|high|max so other providers receive a clean body.

The SSE consumer keeps progress meaningful during long reasoning: reasoning_content deltas hold the percent at the band start while the message reports the live reasoning length, visible content characters map monotonically onto the caller's [start, ceiling] band via streaming_percent, and events are throttled to one per 4096 characters or 1.5 seconds; keep-alives, role-only deltas, and the [DONE] sentinel are ignored.

Stream failures are actionable and preserve the provider's message: an in-stream error payload raises immediately, HTTP failures carry the status code and the first 500 characters of the body, URLError carries the underlying reason, and an empty document names its finish_reason — `length` and `content_filter` get dedicated operator-facing text; every RuntimeError reaches the host as one ENGINE_ERROR protocol event.
A code fence that wraps the whole document is stripped from the finished minutes, while inner code fences of a plain document are preserved.

The prompt contract forbids invention: decisions, owners, dates, and real names must be evidence-backed, speaker labels are never promoted to roster-external real names (uncertain mappings are written as estimates with a confidence note), cross-chunk uncertainty is marked `확인 필요`, sensitive strings such as tokens and keys are masked as `[민감정보 생략]`, and empty sections keep their titles with `해당 없음` — the map prompt repeats the no-guessing and no-invented-names rules per chunk.

minutes_template.py's SYSTEM_PROMPT is the single source of truth for the minutes Markdown structure (status header line, TL;DR, meeting purpose, fielded decisions, action board, per-topic discussion, follow-ups, risks/open questions, and a correction appendix with term and speaker mappings), and both the single-pass prompt and the reduce pass use it, keeping short and long meetings' minutes interchangeable downstream.

When a host-derived meeting date exists, the prompt states it as the estimated date (회의 추정일, 녹음 파일 기준) and instructs the model to use it unless the transcript contains explicit contrary date evidence; with no date the line is omitted entirely rather than left blank.

Imported transcripts refine through the identical path as transcribed meetings — same use case, claim rules, worker command, and prompts, with minutes registered onto the import's job id — but they carry source_audio: None, so no --meeting-date is passed and the transcript's own mtime dates the minutes.

The `refined` protocol event completes the refinement job in the frontend reducer (phase writing, percent 100, message 회의록을 저장했습니다), and after the IPC promise resolves renderMinutes replaces the progress block with the minutes row, enabling the open-minutes action; the reducer also clamps same-phase percent regressions with Math.max so displayed progress is monotonic.

One refinement run follows a fixed progress ladder: 10% while reading the transcript, 35–88% for single-pass streaming, 35–68% for the map band, 70–88% for reduce, 90% before the atomic write, and 100% at the refined event.

Host-side application tests pin the refinement contract: the trimmed key and model/base-url/effort passthrough with background text, roster-ordered attendees, and the full glossary; ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING when no key is saved; imported transcripts refinable without transcription; and the Refined event captured as the process result.

Worker contract tests pin strategy routing exactly at the 48,000-character boundary, lossless whole-turn chunking with preamble carry and context-only marking, shared rounded map-band boundaries, SSE parsing of keep-alives/error payloads/[DONE], reasoning-only progress, finish-reason errors, GLM-versus-other request bodies, fence stripping, and meeting-date anchoring.

The frontend backend port exposes the refinement as BackendPort.refineTranscript, which the Tauri adapter forwards to the Application use case; AppController.refine is the only webview caller and takes its attendee ids from the ParticipantPickerView, which re-applies retainSelection on every roster change so a stale chip selection cannot survive into a request.
